solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artist runs house, in principle, contrarily

indicators.note: in says the runs and house letters go inside the other piece
contrarily asks for the word for principle to be turned the other way round

parts.note: a law is a principle, as in a law of nature
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A painter who runs a home is said to work against his own rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrarily' turns the principle round to WAL; 'in' sets the runs and house letters within it. 'runs' looks like a verb but is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol was the American pop artist famous for soup-can and Marilyn prints.

clue.text: Songstress said real men oddly unavailable

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters unavailable, only the even letters of the phrase remain

explanation.surface: A female singer is reported to be off-limits to genuine men.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of SAIDREALMEN, leaving the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is the multi-award-winning English singer, a songstress by any measure.

clue.text: Chat about head of broadsheet in journalist's car

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters sit inside the word for a journalist

parts.note: a hack is slang for a journalist

indicators.note: about signals the letters of chat and the B are shaken up
head of picks out the first letter of broadsheet

explanation.surface: A conversation about a newspaper's editor takes place in a reporter's vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' mixes the letters of chat with B to make TCHBA, and 'in' sits that within the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a type of car with a rear door that swings upward.

clue.text: Recording about immorality shows behind

indicators.note: about says the word for recording goes around the other piece

parts.note: a log is a record or recording of events
sin is immoral behaviour

explanation.surface: A recorded document reveals the misconduct going on behind the scenes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition but is the definition: a team trailing on the scoreboard is behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A side that is behind in a game is currently trailing, not winning.

clue.text: Wipe over arm edging that's in dirty colour

indicators.note: over asks for the word for wipe to be turned round

parts.note: to rub something is to wipe it
a gun is an arm, a weapon

indicators.note: edging picks out the outer letters of dirty

explanation.surface: Instructions to wipe a sleeve whose edges are stained a grimy shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RUB into BUR; 'edging' takes D and Y, the outside letters of 'dirty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgundy is a deep purplish-red shade named after the wine region.

clue.text: Perhaps fare at Christmas, as EU delegates here, shoots up

parts.note: Brussels is home to the main European Union institutions, where its delegates gather
sprouts means shoots up, as a plant grows

explanation.surface: A seasonal dinner scene as European officials gather and something grows quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as one example of festive food.
explanation.definitionFit: The small green cabbages are a traditional, much-mocked side dish at a British Christmas dinner.

clue.text: Port stirred into Italian food

parts.note: Riga is the Baltic port and capital of Latvia

indicators.note: stirred says the letters of the word into are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fortified wine is mixed into a dish from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink; it is the city of RIGA. 'stirred' rearranges INTO into TONI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ridged tube-shaped pasta from Italy.

clue.text: Doorman sees drug-dealer quietly leaving

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for quietly departs from the dealer word

parts.note: a pusher is someone who sells illegal drugs
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A doorman spots a drug dealer slipping away without a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes P from PUSHER.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats or acts as a doorkeeper at an entrance.

clue.text: Hall of residence staff redirected Mick, half-cut on right wing

indicators.note: redirected says the word for staff is pointed the other way

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

indicators.note: half-cut keeps just the first half of the name Mick

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the right-wing British Conservative party

explanation.surface: University staff send a tipsy Mick back to the right side of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' turns ROD into DOR; 'half-cut' (slang for drunk) keeps MI of Mick.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormitory is a building of sleeping quarters for students, so a hall of residence.

clue.text: Battle site gunners ignored aimless strategy by returning victuals

indicators.note: aimless says the remaining letters wander into a new order
ignored says the gunners' letters are dropped from strategy

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners

indicators.note: returning asks for the food word to be read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food, victuals

explanation.surface: Artillerymen disregard pointless tactics and bring back the rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' takes RA from STRATEGY, leaving STTEGY; 'aimless' rearranges it to GETTYS. 'returning' turns GRUB into BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, saw a decisive 1863 American Civil War battle.

clue.text: Group of women endlessly rabbit?

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a harem is the women of a household in some cultures

explanation.surface: A gathering of women who never stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' as British slang means chatter, fitting the surface; the question mark flags the animal as an example of the answer rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare is a long-eared animal resembling a rabbit, so the query marks a loose example.

clue.text: Alcohol restricts the source of one's writing, according to author

indicators.note: restricts says the alcohol word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: meths, methylated spirits, is a kind of alcohol
ink is what a pen writes with

explanation.surface: A writer's drinking habit limits their creative output.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the author or setter is ME, so the expression means 'in this writer's view'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase means it seems to me, an opinion offered by the speaker or writer.

clue.text: Discover, with one representing university later, a root vegetable

indicators.note: representing, with later, says the letter for one stands in for the second university letter

parts.note: to turn up something is to discover it
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Uncovering, with a later scholar's help, a vegetable from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' points to the second U of TURNUP being replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a round white root grown as a vegetable.

clue.text: Dance that expresses joy and spirit

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of triumph or joy
the ka is the spirit or soul in ancient Egyptian belief

explanation.surface: A dance that conveys happiness and energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is a Maori ceremonial war dance, famously performed by the New Zealand rugby team.

clue.text: US writer left to take a breather, partly in agreed surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the agreed word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: ay is an old word for yes, agreed
to exhale is to breathe out, one part of taking a breath

explanation.surface: An author departs for a rest, partly in pleasant surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a breather' wants to mean rest; here it means breathing, and 'partly' says only the out-breath is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex Haley was the American author of Roots and The Autobiography of Malcolm X.

clue.text: Legendary horseman finds clean ground by chance

indicators.note: ground, as in crushed, says the letters of clean are broken up

parts.note: lot means chance, as in casting lots

explanation.surface: A mythical rider discovers that the soil has been purified by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as earth but signals rearranging CLEAN into LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was the Knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Animated character turning red, fumed about learner driver

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the learner letter
turning says the letters of red and fumed are turned about into a new order

parts.note: L is the plate marking a learner driver

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure going red with rage over a novice motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges REDFUMED into E...MERFUDD, and 'about' wraps it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer Fudd is the hapless hunter who chases Bugs Bunny in Looney Tunes cartoons.

clue.text: Breaking ranks with Abe Lincoln here

indicators.note: breaking says the letters of ranks and Abe are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Breaking ranks alongside President Abraham Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abe Lincoln' looks like one name, but Abe is fodder and Lincoln is the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is the state capital of Nebraska, so the city is found there.

clue.text: Weak spot, lacking resistance by paramilitary unit

indicators.note: lacking says the resistance letter is missing from the spot word

parts.note: a freckle is a small spot on the skin
R is the physics symbol for resistance
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A vulnerable point with no opposition from a militia group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes R from FRECKLE to give FECKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Feckless means lacking strength of character or effectiveness, so ineffectual.

clue.text: Dressing boy amuses some looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A salad sauce that a lad finds entertaining, glancing behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns the hidden OYAM round.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is short for mayonnaise, a common salad dressing.

clue.text: Positively assert broadcast should contain very loud male

indicators.note: should contain says the broadcast word holds the very loud letters

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Confidently claim that a radio programme ought to include a booming man.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to state firmly or declare something to be true.

clue.text: Nag lothario?

definitions.meaning: a nag is a horse, here a racehorse that runs over fences
a lothario is a womaniser who pursues women

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' suggests pestering, but it is a horse: a steeplechaser.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a horse trained for steeplechasing, and also a man who chases women.

clue.text: Upset girl covering 'North and South' (= mouth, an example of such)

indicators.note: covering says the turned girl word wraps around the north letter
upset, in a down clue, says the girl word is turned upside down

parts.note: gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: An annoyed girl hides her mouth, explained in rhyming slang.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'North and South' means mouth, so it is itself an example of the answer. 'Upset' turns GAL into LAG; 'covering' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang is a kind of informal non-standard vocabulary, so the phrase is an instance of it.

clue.text: Commoners repeated phrase loudly after service

indicators.note: after says the loudly letter follows the service

parts.note: a riff is a short repeated musical phrase
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
F, forte, is the musical marking for loudly

explanation.surface: A musical motif played loud once church service is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a church service; it is the armed service RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Riff-raff are the common people, disreputable or of low social class.

clue.text: River Swale's banks treacherous

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

indicators.note: banks, the edges of a river, picks out the outer letters

explanation.surface: The edges of the Swale, a Yorkshire river, are dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The Swale is a river in Yorkshire; its 'banks' are its outside letters S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: False means disloyal or deceitful, as a treacherous friend is.

clue.text: Appeal, as Kent's tail-ender leaves crease

indicators.note: leaves says the tail-ender letter departs from the crease word

parts.note: a pleat is a fold or crease in fabric
the last letter of Kent is T

explanation.surface: A cricket appeal as a Kent lower-order batsman walks off from the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-ender' and 'crease' are cricket terms (a weak late batsman; the batting line) but here mean a last letter and a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is an earnest request or appeal for something.

clue.text: Boss adheres to financial promise — shrewd in an academic way

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised ornamental knob
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt
sly means cunning or shrewd

explanation.surface: A manager clings to a loan pledge, astute in a scholarly fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager; it is a knob or stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Studiously means with diligent attention to study, so in a scholarly manner.

clue.text: Reader's assistant easily disheartened, say, by young lady

indicators.note: disheartened says the heart is removed, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman readily discouraged helps out with reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle of 'easily', leaving EY.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens or monocle that helps someone to read.

clue.text: Refuse to convert grey study

indicators.note: to convert says the word for grey is turned around

parts.note: dim means grey or dull
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Declining to transform a drab study room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish. 'to convert' turns DIM into MID.
explanation.definitionFit: A midden is a dunghill or heap of household waste.
